---
title: "Adopt the Pet"
---

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will run a small local model with Ollama, give it enough context, and point OpenCode at it.
- **Before you start:** [Save Point](../crypt/shield-of-undo.html); a laptop with about 16 GB of memory; a terminal; roughly 5 GB of free disk. OpenCode is an open-source coding agent that can use local models.
- **Time:** about 20 minutes. Everything stays on your machine.
:::

A small local model is gentle, free, and private. It forgets quickly, so check its answers before you rely on them.

## 1. Install Ollama and fetch a model

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh     # macOS and Linux
ollama pull qwen3:4b                              # about 2.5 GB
ollama run qwen3:4b "Say hello in one sentence."
```

`qwen3:4b` is one example of a small model that Ollama lists with tool support. Model names change quickly, so check the "tools" badge on the model's page at ollama.com/library. Run `ollama ps` while it runs to see what loaded and whether it fits your RAM (ordinary memory).

WSL (Windows Subsystem for Linux) users: run the Linux commands inside your WSL terminal, and check each tool's current docs if one fails.

## 2. Give it room to think

The context length (also called the context window: how much text the model can see at once) defaults to **4k tokens** in Ollama on machines with under 24 GiB of video memory (VRAM, the memory on the graphics card or shared with it). That includes a 16 GB laptop. Agents and coding tools need **at least 64k**; OpenCode requires 64k or higher. Set it when you start the server:

```bash
OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=64000 ollama serve
```

Check what loaded with `ollama ps`. A bigger context needs more memory. Look at the PROCESSOR column: a model that spills onto the CPU (the main processor) runs slower than one that stays on the GPU.

## 3. Point OpenCode at it

Install OpenCode, then connect inside it with `/connect` (a `/command` is typed inside the running tool):

```bash
curl -fsSL https://opencode.ai/v2/install | bash
```

If the install command errors, check the current OpenCode docs for your version.

OpenCode finds Ollama at `http://127.0.0.1:11434` automatically. To spell it out, put this in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "providers": {
    "ollama": { "settings": { "baseURL": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1" } }
  }
}
```

## 4. Put the Pet on a leash

OpenCode's default policy is **allow everything**, except reading `.env` files, which it asks about. Shell commands run with your user's authority, and the shell is not a sandbox. Each rule says `allow` (run without asking), `ask` (prompt you first) or `deny` (never run). A safer start asks about everything first, then narrows. **Rules are checked in order and the last match wins:**

```json
{
  "permissions": [
    { "action": "*", "resource": "*", "effect": "ask" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git status *", "effect": "allow" },
    { "action": "shell", "resource": "git push *", "effect": "deny" }
  ]
}
```

## Other small models to try

Mistral publishes open-weight models that Ollama lists with tool support:

- **`ministral-3`:** 3B (3.0 GB), 8B (6.0 GB) and 14B (9.1 GB) sizes, Apache 2.0.
- **`mistral-small`:** 24B (14 GB), Apache 2.0.

A 24B model needs far more memory than a 3B one, so check `ollama ps` after loading.

## A built-in Pet on newer Macs

Recent Macs ship a small on-device model with the operating system, and developers call it through Apple's Foundation Models framework. Availability depends on whether your device and region support Apple Intelligence, and the model can take a while to download after you turn that on. It suits summarising, extracting and classifying text. It may struggle with basic math, code and logical reasoning.

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [ministral-3](https://ollama.com/library/ministral-3): Ollama library, docs. Why read: it lists the sizes, context length, tool support and licence of a small Mistral model you can pull instead of a Qwen one.
- [OpenCode](https://docs.ollama.com/integrations/opencode): Ollama, docs. Why read: it is the vendor guide to running OpenCode against a local Ollama model, including the context length it needs. It still shows older OpenCode install commands, so check the OpenCode docs too.
- [Providers](https://opencode.ai/docs/providers/): OpenCode, docs. Why read: it shows how to connect Ollama or an OpenAI-compatible gateway in the current config format.
- [Config](https://opencode.ai/docs/config/): OpenCode, docs. Why read: it lists where `opencode.json` lives and how global and project files override each other.
- [Permissions](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/): OpenCode, docs. Why read: it explains how to control what the agent may do, which matters more with a small local model.
- [Foundation Models updates](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/updates/foundationmodels): Apple, docs. Why read: it lists the changes to Apple's on-device model by date, including which OS versions change the model.
- [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode): GitHub, repo. Why read: it is the source and release list, useful when the docs and your installed version disagree.
:::
